items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I was lucky enough to play with some of the greats of the era that I particularly love, like Vic Dickinson and Doc Cheatham

ctx.x: Yeah. But anyway I did accompany a lot of American artists, Pee Wee Russell, Charlie Shavers, Benny Carter, oh it was so nice. But of course when you come here it’s a different story because this country’s so vast. You know you don’t see these people anymore, wherever. But when they came to England — anyway, Red Allen was so encouraging. But I got here in 1980 and started working in New York. There were still a few clubs going there and I started beating around and working in places. But I was lucky enough to…

remember going up to Jule Styne’s apartment and he gave us the song that he kind of, one of the last songs that he’d written and he said we could use it on the album. And of course, sure we’d love to if we could do it, and we did it. And up in his apartment there were paintings by George Gershwin on the wall. You know Gershwin was a very accomplished artist. And he had one of Gershwin’s paintings. And I remember sitting there and the phone rings, and who’s on the other end of the line is Irving Berlin. So I mean…
